summary: Staffed Coast Guard light at the mouth of Templar Channel near Tofino, first lit 1 November 1904 from a wooden octagonal tower; the date of the present fibreglass tower is disputed.

structures.note: 80 ft (24 m) from base to vane; dioptric first-order apparatus; replaced by the fibreglass tower in 1968 (LighthouseFriends).

structures.type: fibreglass tower, round, white with red lantern
structures.note: LighthouseFriends: 4,600 lb, 55 ft, airlifted in 1968. Lighthouse Directory: 18 m (58 ft) and dated 1959.
Built by day labour south of the lighthouse; steam diaphone installed in duplicate.

staffing.note: Head keeper list runs to Martin Mountford (at least 2024). Senate 2010 table: two positions, permanent residents.

access.note: Staffed Coast Guard light where keepers live. Reached by boat; scenic flights from Tofino show the station from the air (LighthouseFriends). Visitors should not land without the Coast Guard's invitation.

visit.grounds_note: LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory describe the site as open and the tower as closed.

events.note: Wooden octagonal tower, dwelling and outbuildings; $10,955.69 by day labour under George Frost (LighthouseFriends).
Fog alarm building erected (Marine report); steam diaphone installed in duplicate, finished December 1905 (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper's dwelling burned to the ground on 24 June 1927; the fire reached the oil house (LighthouseFriends).
New keeper's dwelling built the following year (LighthouseFriends).
Christmas supplies landed in a storm by three fishermen after the Tofino lifeboat could not land (LighthouseFriends, citing the Times Colonist).
Oakes & Wilson contracted to build two single dwellings and demolish two (LighthouseFriends). The Directory gives 1959 for the present tower.
Fibreglass tower airlifted in and set on a concrete pad, replacing the original wooden octagonal tower (LighthouseFriends).
Minor damage to the waiting tower when a private aircraft collided with it at Tofino airport, ten days before installation (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.why: The 1904 tower was a wooden octagonal building 80 ft (24 m) to the vane (Marine report 1904; LighthouseFriends). The 18 m height belongs to the later fibreglass tower, which the record dates to 1904.

corrections.proposed: merge with the present fibreglass tower entry
corrections.why: The OpenStreetMap entry duplicates the present tower; the Directory and LighthouseFriends both describe a single present tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Structure positions in the record differ by more than 500 m. The Coast Guard's list position (49 06 37.5 N, 125 55 24.7 W) matches LighthouseFriends' coordinates and the record's point, so the Coast Guard list is taken as the position of the light.

notes_for_editor: The 1904 report is primary and clear. The 1903, 1905 and 1906 Marine entries come from the corpus. The 1903 clearing sentence ('burned at a cost of $1,120') is on printed p. 72 (scan p. 85); the proposal sentence starts on scan p. 84, whose printed page is not confirmed. The 1905 fog-alarm entry sits under the heading 'New Aids to Navigation', British Columbia, not 'Changes and Improvements'. The 1906 keeper list (printed p. 176, scan p. 185) is an OCR table matched by position. The page image was checked in the Internet Archive viewer: 'Garrard, F. C' sits on the same row as 'Lennard Island'. The 1907 report (scan p. 155, printed p. 148) shows the same pairing in its own OCR. The present tower's date is disputed: LighthouseFriends dates the airlifted fibreglass tower to 1968; the Lighthouse Directory dates the present tower to 1959 with no source given. The story follows LighthouseFriends and says the sources disagree; the Directory's 1959 may refer to the 1959 dwellings contract, which the story flags only as possible. Editor may check a Coast Guard or Marine record for 1959 to 1968 if one is found; the local corpus stops at fiscal 1924. Most of the keeper life, the 1927 fire, the 1908 family death and the 1932 Christmas delivery come from LighthouseFriends (copyrighted: facts restated in our words, with one short quotation). Edward's death: LighthouseFriends says he picked up what was taken for sugar and swallowed lye; the story says he swallowed lye that he had taken for sugar. The Times Colonist was not read directly and is footnoted second-hand. The three fishermen of 1932 are not named. LighthouseFriends' 1995 article about the Holland family names a child; he is not named here. Keeper names after about 1960 come only from LighthouseFriends' published list. The Chance Heritage Trust page reproduces LighthouseFriends' text and is not used as a source. Shared names across LighthouseFriends lists (Arthur Ernest Kelly at Pine Island; Martin Mountford at Bonilla Island) are not linked. The 1904 report and the Directory give distances in 'miles' without saying nautical miles; the story keeps the report's word. The Coast Guard list number for Lennard Island is 134 (intl. G5242), not 1407.
